title: Terraform State and Remote Backend
description: Move Terraform state into Azure Storage with locking so concurrent pipeline runs cannot corrupt it.

data.text: A developer ran `terraform apply` from their laptop while a pipeline run was applying simultaneously. The state file is now inconsistent, `terraform plan` wants to recreate the production SQL server, and nobody has a backup of the previous state. Fix the workflow.

Use a **remote backend on Azure Storage** with **blob lease locking**, and make the pipeline the only place `apply` runs. Enable **blob versioning** and **soft delete** on the state container so a corrupted or overwritten state file can be recovered. Split environments into separate state keys so a dev mistake cannot touch production state.

data.title: Bootstrap the state storage account
data.code:
az group create --name rg-tfstate --location westeurope

az storage account create \
  --name sttfstatequotient \
  --resource-group rg-tfstate \
  --sku Standard_ZRS \
  --encryption-services blob \
  --min-tls-version TLS1_2

# Data protection: versioning + soft delete make state recoverable
az storage account blob-service-properties update \
  --account-name sttfstatequotient \
  --enable-versioning true \
  --enable-delete-retention true \
  --delete-retention-days 30

az storage container create --name tfstate --account-name sttfstatequotient

data.title: backend.tf — remote state with locking

data.text: Local state is a single mutable file with no concurrency control and no audit trail. Two simultaneous applies will both read a stale snapshot and write back conflicting results — which is exactly how a plan ends up "recreating" infrastructure that already exists. A leased blob lets the second runner fail fast instead of corrupting the world.
